preamble: All the across solutions are of a kind and may not be further defined.

clue.text: My own dear son is the one to shield a criminal

parts.note: surface padding that sets up the doting parent

indicators.note: a shield conceals what lies behind it, so the letters are kept out of sight in the words

parts.note: the letters run on across these words, from the end of the first to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A doting parent insists their beloved boy is the one to protect a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a search for a word meaning son, but the answer is concealed in plain sight, straddling four consecutive words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately sets fire to property commits a crime, so this person is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: One people saying they …

definitions.note: the definition runs on into the next clue: a word said to show the speakers agree

parts.note: a means one
men are people

explanation.surface: A sentence about what a nation says, broken off to be finished by the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue with the next: read together, the definition is 'saying they agree', the word a congregation says at the end of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Congregations utter this word at the close of prayers to signal assent, so it is literally speech expressing accord.

clue.text: … agree with a dog

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for 'with'
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a people who see eye to eye with a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but supplies the letters, as con is 'with' in Italian (as in con brio).
explanation.definitionFit: To be of one mind, or hold the same opinion as someone else, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: H as for Hook, for example

parts.note: taken as written
Captain Hook is the pirate villain of Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Reads like a spelling alphabet: H as in Hook.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like the phonetic 'H for Hook', but Hook is an example of a pirate, and the letter H is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoneticians call the breathy sound of the letter h an aspirate, a consonant pronounced with an audible puff of breath.

clue.text: Exchanging gems with tin, His Highness is with it

indicators.note: exchanging swaps letters about, so they end in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy royal swapping his jewels for cheap metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His Highness' reads as one title, but 'His' is part of the letters to rearrange and 'Highness' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'His Mightiness' was an old honorific for a ruler, comparable to the royal title used for princes.

clue.text: Could be a second and many of them

definitions.meaning: a second-class honours award from a university is one kind
an angular unit is made up of thousands of seconds of arc

explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to 'a second': one sense is a university award graded first, second and so on; the other is the unit of angle split into 3,600 arc seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an academic qualification classed by grade and an angular measure subdivided into minutes and seconds.

clue.text: Steak that holds a memory

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a T-bone is a cut of steak
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A dinner that brings back recollections.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says every across answer is the same kind of thing, a musical instrument, so no definition is given.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument with a sliding tube is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.

clue.text: Old part of bridge ruled out?

definitions.note: read as 'one who ruled out in the provinces', a noun

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an arch is a span of a bridge

explanation.surface: A section of an old bridge that is now excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruled out' looks like 'excluded', but it means governed away from the centre: an exarch was a Byzantine provincial governor.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine emperors sent these governors to rule distant provinces such as Ravenna, far from Constantinople.

clue.text: Group drinking a quantity of beer

indicators.note: something drinking takes the drink inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a set is a group
a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons of beer

explanation.surface: A party sinking a lot of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin is an old British brewing measure, half a firkin.
explanation.definitionFit: This small harpsichord-type keyboard is one of the musical instruments the preamble calls for.

clue.text: See 22
Verse: that which circulated among Olympians dressed to go out

indicators.note: clothes go on the outside of the wearer, so this piece goes round the others

parts.note: clad means dressed
V is the abbreviation for verse
ichor is the fluid said to flow in the veins of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: Poetry about the drink passed round the gods, who were dressed for an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Olympians are the gods of Mount Olympus, not athletes; what circulated among them is their blood, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This early keyboard, whose strings are struck by metal tangents, is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.

clue.text: Lady on the spot

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it, so the order is flipped

parts.note: a zit is a pimple, a spot
her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: A woman who arrives immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the spot' looks like 'immediately', but spot means a pimple; in an across answer 'on' puts the lady after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat stringed box, plucked while lying on a table, is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.

clue.text: My bill hung badly, so that my pride was hurt

definitions.text: so that my pride was hurt

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed when an invoice, or a beak, drooped in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverbial phrase, so it describes how something was done: in a way that dented one's pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a manner that makes a person feel small and lowers their self-esteem is done in a deflating way.

clue.text: Blood circulating at home

indicators.note: to circulate is to go round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: claret is old boxing slang for blood
in means at home

explanation.surface: Describes blood flowing round the body, or round a household.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is a red Bordeaux wine, and from its colour British slang for blood, especially in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-reed woodwind is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.

clue.text: Pig stealer gets beaten

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme thief, the piper's son who stole a pig and ran away
the rhyme ends with the boy beaten, and a drum is something struck

explanation.surface: A thief caught and punished.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son, stole a pig and away he run; the pig was eat, and Tom was beat'. The drum is the instrument the preamble asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy of the nursery rhyme is named twice, and the same doubled name is a hand-struck drum.

clue.text: Too much given to harrying of vendor

indicators.note: harrying is harassing and ravaging, which leaves the letters in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone overly inclined to pester a street seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' means inclined to, so the definition is an adjective phrase, as in 'too much given to drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively keen on or attached to something is being inclined to it beyond reason.

clue.text: Call again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a beck is a beckoning call, as in 'at one's beck and call'

explanation.surface: A request to phone back.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the opposite order to the clue. A rebeck (or rebec) is a medieval bowed stringed instrument, the one the preamble asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped medieval fiddle, played with a bow, is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.

clue.text: King meets newsagent about the last sonata

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: Reuters is the news agency founded by Paul Reuter
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A monarch encountering a shopkeeper who sells papers, regarding a final piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newsagent' looks like a corner-shop owner, but read as 'news agent' it is the agency Reuters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Violin Sonata No. 9 is known by this name, after the violinist Rodolphe Kreutzer to whom it was dedicated.

clue.text: Cross high-sounding bridge? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of something means its ending falls short
sounding means as heard, so the letters follow the pronunciation, not the spelling

parts.note: spelt by sound
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a grand-sounding bridge, or crossing one, only partway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb, as in crossing a bridge, but it is the noun: a hybrid is a cross between two breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or animal bred from two different varieties is called a cross, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Exposure of spy should encompass change

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so one piece goes round the other
exposing an agent turns him out, and turning out rearranges letters

parts.note: taken as written
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Unmasking a secret agent ought to bring about reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged spy wraps round the word for change. The psaltery is an ancient plucked stringed instrument, the one the preamble asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient plucked stringed instrument, mentioned in the Psalms, is one of those the preamble asks for.

clue.text: A shade animated?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ghost, as the shades of the dead

definitions.note: an adjective for the quality the noun names; spirit is what makes something animated
definitions.meaning: second meaning: liveliness, the life that animates a body

explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade' looks like a colour; it is the classical word for a ghost. The question mark admits that the second sense is the quality, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a ghost of the departed and the vivacity or soul that brings a body to life.

clue.text: Rendering Shaw as critic, live, at the point where Fool enters

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: to be is to live
an ass is a fool
a thorn is a sharp point

explanation.surface: Translating a playwright's criticism vividly at the moment the jester comes on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw wrote music criticism as 'Corno di Bassetto', Italian for this instrument; rendering that pen name into English gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's Italian pen name translates literally as this alto clarinet, so rendering it into English gives the instrument.

clue.text: Example of business outlet for German car?

parts.note: the bee is the proverbial example of busyness, as in 'busy as a bee'
split as 'out' plus 'let', with 'out' meaning out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dealership selling a German car is a model of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' is read as busy-ness, the bee's quality, and 'outlet' splits into 'out' and 'let'. The question mark marks the car as a nickname, not a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Volkswagen's rounded small car is popularly named after the insect, so the name fits the German vehicle.

clue.text: Ottoman government detaining Scotsman of paradoxical type

indicators.note: to detain is to hold in custody, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: the Sublime Porte was the name for the Ottoman government
Ian is the typical Scottish man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Turkish state imprisoning a Scot who is a contradictory sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is part of the inserted letters. The name of the instrument means 'soft-loud' in Italian, which is why it is a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Its name joins the Italian words for soft and loud, two opposites, so the instrument is self-contradictory by name.

clue.text: It can be riven

parts.note: surface reading: anything that can be split apart
setter's reading: Tennyson's line about 'the little rift within' a stringed instrument that makes the music mute

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to Tennyson's 'It is the little rift within the lute, / That by and by will make the music mute'; the preamble supplies the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped plucked stringed instrument is the one Tennyson pictured with a small crack spoiling its sound.

clue.text: Lion starts to open window at home?

definitions.note: a home is where something is at; the question mark admits the noun is reached loosely

indicators.note: where something starts is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to air a room is to open the window

explanation.surface: A big cat begins to push open a window in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' looks like 'begins to', but only 'starts' acts on the big cat; 'to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is where it lives, so this word names a beast's dwelling place.

clue.text: Dip some olives in Sauterne, say

indicators.note: to dip one thing into another is to put it inside

parts.note: vin is French for wine, and Sauterne is a French wine

indicators.note: some of a thing is only part of it, so just the opening letters are used

parts.note: only the first letters, the start of the word, are kept

explanation.surface: A dining instruction: soak a few olives in a sweet white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauterne(s) is a sweet French white wine, and the French word for wine supplies the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This four-stringed bowed instrument, the highest of its family, is one of those the preamble asks for.

clue.text: Boring slow boil, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the words, so the answer follows their pronunciation

parts.note: boring is dull and a slow boil is a simmer

explanation.surface: A cook complaining that watching a pan bubble gently is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the two words for boring and gentle boiling run into the instrument's name, which the preamble defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This trapezoid stringed instrument struck with small hammers is one of the musical instruments the preamble asks for.
